title: Adaptive token compactor and shadow-kernel routing for Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks
author: Elena Martinez
release_notes: Adds an optional token compactor for the KV cache that reduces fragmentation for MQA/GQA models; introduces a shadow-kernel routing path that prefers low-stride kernels for odd head configurations; exposes new runtime metrics (kv_compactor_* and kernel_shadow_routing_*); default disabled for Private installs; opt-in via runtime config.
description: Context: Some Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants expose pathological head/stride combinations that cause our default kernel selection to perform suboptimally and cause inflated KV cache footprint for interleaved multi-query (MQA/GQA) workloads. Motivation: reduce per-token cost and P95 latency regressions in long-chat and streaming scenarios without changing model weights or upstream tokenization. What this PR does: 1) Token compactor: a lightweight in-memory compaction pass that coalesces contiguous KV slots created by interleaved MQA dispatches. Compactor runs incrementally on write paths and during idle GC windows; it is configurable by budget/threshold and avoids compaction for hot prefixes. 2) Shadow-kernel routing: a secondary kernel selection path that is probed when the primary kernel has a stride mismatch cost estimate > threshold. The shadow path prefers kernels with packed memory access or head-stride-friendly tiling and falls back automatically. 3) Telemetry: adds kv_compactor_run_count, kv_compactor_evictions, kernel_shadow_probes, kernel_shadow_accepts, and per-model histograms for compaction latency. 4) Safety and opt-in: feature gated behind runtime config (runtime.features.token_compactor, runtime.features.shadow_kernel_routing). Default disabled for Private instals; enabled behind runtime flag for Hosted and Dedicated for initial rollout. Design notes: compactor uses lock-free slab iteration with epoch guards to avoid blocking inference path; we keep a conservative per-model budget to avoid eviction storms. Shadow routing computes a quick heuristic (stride_penalty + head_mismatch_score) and issues a single shadow probe per request up to a configurable probe window to limit overhead. Testing & validation: microbenchmarks (unit + e2e) added; stress tests on long chat traces (100k+ tokens) and hybrid MQA/GQA mixes. Results: Llama-7B MQA: 11.8% throughput increase, 9.7% P95 latency reduction; Mistral-7B mixed: 6-8% token cost decrease; Qwen-14B edge traces: 3.4% reduction in token cache size with negligible cold-start penalty. Rollout plan: start with Hosted opt-in customers, smoke for Dedicated tenants with telemetry, then enable by default after two weeks if no regression. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf harness runs - [x] docs & runtime config - [x] Telemetry dashboards created - [x] Security review (no secret handling) Related: ENG-7321 (kv fragmentation investigation), ENG-7432 (kernel-routing heuristics).

For Dedicated/private, enable via runtime.features.token_compactor=true and runtime.features.shadow_kernel_routing=true with conservative budget: runtime.kv_compactor_budget=0.02 (2% global memory).
